title: Black sliding wallpaper on activity change
line: Switching activities now slides the new wallpaper in over the old one instead of over a black screen.
explanation: When the activity changes, ContainmentView (libplasma) hides the old containment right away, but Desktop.qml then runs its slide animation as if the old one were still there, so the new wallpaper slid in over black. For an activity shown for the first time, its containment and wallpaper are only created at that moment, so the screen stayed black until the image had loaded (about 2 s on the rig). Desktop.qml now shows the old containment again for the switch, keeps the new one off screen until its uiReady (wallpaper loaded) is true, and only then slides it in.

commits.message:
desktop: keep the old activity visible until the new one slides in

The view hides the old containment as soon as the activity changes, so
the screen went black while the new activity loaded and it slid in over
black. Keep the old one shown and start the slide once the new is ready.

BUG: 452104

media.caption: First switch to a new activity: the screen goes black until its wallpaper loads
First switch: the old desktop stays until the new one is ready, then it slides in
Switching to an activity with another wallpaper: it slides in over black
The new wallpaper slides in over the old one

reviews.text: This cleanly fixes both the black flash while a new activity's wallpaper loads and the slide-over-black transition by re-showing the old containment in Desktop.qml and parking the new containment off-screen until its plasmoid reports isUiReady. Edge cases around interrupting a pending switch and switching back to the still-visible old containment are properly handled without breaking other ContainmentView users, and the before/after frame strips confirm zero black frames.

ContainmentView hides the old containment as soon as the activity changes, so Desktop.qml's slide always ran over black, and a first-time activity also slid in before its wallpaper existed; re-showing the old containment and starting switchAnim only once the new containment's isUiReady is true fixes both cases from the report, and the frame strips show the new wallpaper sliding over the old one with no black frame. The edge cases are handled carefully: a pending switch to a containment that is not ready yet is cancelled when another switch arrives, and switching back to the still-shown desktop no longer hides it. Nitpick: there is no fallback if a third-party wallpaper never clears `loading` (the old desktop would stay until it does); a short safety timeout that starts the slide anyway would make this bulletproof, but the stock image wallpaper clears loading on error too, so it is not blocking.
